steps.note: Remove any leftover (possibly INVALID) index from an earlier failed attempt so the build below starts clean. No-op today; CONCURRENTLY so it never blocks the app's reads or writes.
steps.sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS orders_customer_id_idx;

steps.note: Build the index online. CONCURRENTLY takes only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, so inserts and reads keep running during the build. (customer_id, id) serves GET /customer/C (WHERE customer_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10) straight from the index with no sort. Kept alone in its own step because CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block.
steps.sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_idx ON orders (customer_id, id);

steps.note: Check that the index is VALID (a concurrent build that fails part-way leaves an invalid index behind). Stop the plan with an error if it is not.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_index WHERE indexrelid = 'public.orders_customer_id_idx'::regclass AND indisvalid AND indisready) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders_customer_id_idx is not valid'; END IF; END $$;
